off.name: autocomplete
off.description: Complete a partial address or administrative-area prefix into full valid addresses (e.g. "stat" -> "State Capitol, ..."). Use for prefix completion as the user types; use autosuggest for typo-tolerant fuzzy suggestions and geocode_forward for a full address. Parameters: query (required); optional near {latitude, longitude}, radius_m (with near), country_codes, bounding_box {west, south, east, north}, limit, language, view. Example: {"query": "stat", "near": {"latitude": 35.4769, "longitude": -97.4872}, "limit": 5}

near.description: Center of the search context; results are ranked around this point

radius_m.description: With `near`: hard-limit results to this radius in meters

country_codes.description: Restrict results to these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, e.g. ["USA","MEX"])

bounding_box.description: Hard-limit results to this bounding box

language.description: Result language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US"

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

off.name: autosuggest
off.description: Suggest address and place candidates from an incomplete or misspelled query (typo-tolerant, e.g. "aqaurium" still matches aquariums). Use for search-as-you-type; use autocomplete for strict prefix completion of valid addresses. Parameters: query (required); optional near {latitude, longitude}, radius_m (with near), country_codes, bounding_box {west, south, east, north}, limit, language, view. Example: {"query": "aqauriums", "near": {"latitude": 42.3501, "longitude": -71.0689}, "limit": 5}

near.description: Center of the search context; results are ranked around this point

radius_m.description: With `near`: hard-limit results to this radius in meters

country_codes.description: Restrict results to these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, e.g. ["USA","MEX"])

bounding_box.description: Hard-limit results to this bounding box

language.description: Result language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US"

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

off.name: bbox
off.description: The smallest latitude/longitude box around a set of points, a line or a polygon, optionally padded in metres — for example a viewport for static_map_image or a spatial filter. Handles shapes that straddle the antimeridian (reports crosses_antimeridian and the narrower box). Computed locally, no sign-in needed. Parameters: exactly one of points (array of {latitude, longitude}), line (array of points) or polygon (GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon, isochrone Feature accepted); padding_meters (default 0). Returns min_latitude, min_longitude, max_latitude, max_longitude, crosses_antimeridian. Example: {"points": [{"latitude": 12.9716, "longitude": 77.5946}, {"latitude": 13.0827, "longitude": 80.2707}], "padding_meters": 500}

id.description: Optional label echoed back in the result

line.description: A line as an array of {latitude, longitude} points (at least 2)

polygon.description: A GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon geometry (coordinates in [longitude, latitude] order), or a Feature wrapping one — an isochrone contour can be passed as is

padding_meters.description: Grow the box by this many metres on every side

off.name: buffer
off.description: Build the zone within a given straight-line distance of a point (a circle), a line (a corridor, e.g. 1 km along a route) or a polygon (grown outward, or shrunk inward with a negative distance). Geodesic on WGS84, computed locally, no sign-in needed. Returns a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon (a shrunk shape may split) with its area; an empty result is returned, not an error. Parameters: exactly one of point ({latitude, longitude}), line (array of points) or polygon (GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon, isochrone Feature accepted); distance (number, negative only for polygon); units (default meters); steps (points per circle, default 16); area_units; max_vertices (default 500). Example: {"line": [{"latitude": 12.9716, "longitude": 77.5946}, {"latitude": 12.99, "longitude": 77.62}], "distance": 1, "units": "kilometers"}

point.description: Buffer around a point (a geodesic circle)

polygon.description: Buffer around or inside a polygon

distance.description: Buffer distance; negative shrinks a polygon inward

steps.description: Vertices per quarter... per full circle (default 16)

max_vertices.description: Simplify the returned shape to at most this many vertices (default 500); the result says when it was simplified

off.name: centroid
off.description: The area-weighted centre of a polygon and a label point that is guaranteed to lie inside it (the centroid of a C- or ring-shaped area falls outside; the label point does not). Computed locally, no sign-in needed. Parameters: polygon (GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon, or an isochrone Feature). Returns centroid, label_point ({latitude, longitude}) and centroid_inside. Example: {"polygon": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[77.59, 12.97], [77.61, 12.97], [77.61, 12.99], [77.59, 12.99], [77.59, 12.97]]]}}

polygon.description: A GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon geometry (coordinates in [longitude, latitude] order), or a Feature wrapping one — an isochrone contour can be passed as is

off.name: directions
off.description: Calculate a route between an origin and a destination with optional waypoints; returns distance (meters), duration (seconds) and an encoded polyline per route, which static_route_map can draw. Use distance_matrix for many pairs. Documentation for this API is available through search_documentation. Parameters: origin, destination {latitude, longitude} (required); optional waypoints (max 200), mode (car | truck | motorcycle | bike | walk), service ("flexible" default: all options; "fast": car/truck only, lower latency), route_type, departure_time, avoid (soft), exclude (strict), road_info, honor_restrictions, alternatives, steps (fast only), geometry (polyline | polyline6), cross_border; truck options: truck_size_cm, truck_weight_kg, truck_axle_load, hazmat_type, emission_class; freight network: prefer "truck_route" + truck_type (rigid_truck | semi_trailer | b_double | road_train | generic_truck) for roads legal for that truck class, require "truck_route" to stay on it. Example: {"origin": {"latitude": 37.7749, "longitude": -122.4194}, "destination": {"latitude": 34.0522, "longitude": -118.2437}, "mode": "truck", "prefer": "truck_route", "truck_type": ["b_double"]}

origin.description: Route start (must be a routable land location)

destination.description: Route end (must be a routable land location)

mode.description: Travel mode (default car). Modes other than car/truck require service=flexible

service.description: API variant: "flexible" (default) supports all modes, departure_time, route_type, full avoid list and truck options; "fast" is lower latency but limited to car/truck and avoid toll/ferry/highway only

departure_time.description: Departure as a UNIX timestamp in seconds, for typical-traffic routing (flexible only)

avoid.description: Road features to avoid when alternatives exist. Fast service supports only toll/ferry/highway

exclude.description: Strict filter: only routes that completely avoid these features are returned (error if none exists). Use `avoid` for a soft preference instead. Flexible service only

road_info.description: Extra per-segment information to return: max_speed, toll_distance, toll_cost, toll_info, truck_route, stop_sign, traffic_light (flexible service only)

hazmat_type.description: Hazardous cargo classes carried (truck mode, flexible service only)

truck_axle_load.description: Load per axle in tonnes (truck mode, flexible service only)

emission_class.description: Engine emission class (EU regions, truck mode, flexible service only)

prefer.description: Prioritise designated freight network roads (flexible service, mode truck). truck_type takes effect only together with this

require.description: Restrict the route to designated freight network roads; the API answers HTTP 422 when no such road is within 2 km of the origin, destination or a waypoint. Needs prefer: "truck_route"

truck_type.description: Truck class(es) the route must be legal for on the designated freight network (rigid_truck, semi_trailer, b_double, road_train, generic_truck). Effective together with prefer: "truck_route" (flexible service, mode truck)

cross_border.description: Allow the route to cross international borders (region-dependent, flexible service only)

honor_restrictions.description: When true, enforce restricted-area rules: no route is generated if origin, destination, or a waypoint is inside a restricted area. Default false: route anyway with a warning (flexible service only)

alternatives.description: Return up to 3 alternative routes (only without waypoints)

geometry.description: Route geometry encoding (default polyline, precision 5 — directly usable with static_route_map)

truck_size_cm.description: Truck dimensions in cm (flexible + mode=truck only)

truck_weight_kg.description: Truck gross weight in kg (flexible + mode=truck only)

off.name: distance_matrix
off.description: Compute travel distance (meters) and duration (seconds) for every origin-to-destination pair in one call; one row per origin with one element per destination, in input order. Use it instead of repeated directions calls when several pairs are needed. Documentation for this API is available through search_documentation. Parameters: origins, destinations (arrays of {latitude, longitude}, required); optional mode, service ("fast" default: up to 1000x1000 points; "flexible": the options below, max 50x50), route_type, departure_time, avoid (soft), exclude (strict), honor_restrictions, route_failed_prompt (unroutable pairs return -1 instead of 0), truck options: truck_size_cm {height, width, length}, truck_weight_kg, truck_axle_load, hazmat_type, emission_class, cross_border, prefer "truck_route" + truck_type (roads legal for a truck class on the designated freight network). Example: {"origins": [{"latitude": 1.29, "longitude": 103.85}], "destinations": [{"latitude": 1.35, "longitude": 103.99}, {"latitude": 1.3, "longitude": 103.77}], "route_failed_prompt": true}

mode.description: Travel mode (default car). Modes other than car/truck require service=flexible

service.description: API variant: "fast" (default) supports up to 1000x1000 points; "flexible" adds departure_time, route_type, truck options and more modes but is limited to 50x50 points within a ~8000 km area

departure_time.description: Departure as a UNIX timestamp in seconds, for typical-traffic results (flexible only)

exclude.description: Strict filter: only routes that completely avoid these features are returned (error if none exists). Use `avoid` for a soft preference instead. Flexible service only

hazmat_type.description: Hazardous cargo classes carried (truck mode, flexible service only)

truck_axle_load.description: Load per axle in tonnes (truck mode, flexible service only)

emission_class.description: Engine emission class (EU regions, truck mode, flexible service only)

prefer.description: Prioritise designated freight network roads (flexible service, mode truck). truck_type takes effect only together with this

truck_type.description: Truck class(es) the route must be legal for on the designated freight network (rigid_truck, semi_trailer, b_double, road_train, generic_truck). Effective together with prefer: "truck_route" (flexible service, mode truck)

cross_border.description: Allow routes to cross international borders (region-dependent, flexible service only)

route_failed_prompt.description: When true, unroutable origin/destination pairs return -1 instead of 0 so they can be told apart from zero-distance pairs

honor_restrictions.description: When true, enforce restricted-area rules for origin/destination points instead of routing through with a warning (flexible service only)

truck_size_cm.description: Truck dimensions in cm (flexible + mode=truck only)

truck_weight_kg.description: Truck gross weight in kg (flexible + mode=truck only)

off.name: geocode_batch
off.description: Forward-geocode up to 100 free-text queries in one request; returns one ranked result set per query, in input order. Use it instead of repeated geocode_forward calls when several addresses are needed: this endpoint has its own rate limit of 60 requests per minute, so larger batches per call stay within it. Parameters: queries (required array; each item: query (required), optional near {latitude, longitude}, radius_m, country_codes, bounding_box, limit, language, view, types); optional top-level types (houseNumber | addressBlock | street | intersection | place | area) as the default for all queries (a per-query types overrides it). Example: {"queries": [{"query": "600-699 Golden Gate Ave, San Francisco, CA", "types": ["addressBlock"]}, {"query": "Empire State Building", "country_codes": ["USA"]}]}

query.description: Free-text search query for this entry

near.description: Center of the search context; results are ranked around this point

radius_m.description: With `near`: hard-limit results to this radius in meters

country_codes.description: Restrict results to these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, e.g. ["USA","MEX"])

bounding_box.description: Hard-limit results to this bounding box

language.description: Result language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US"

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

types.description: Restrict results to these types: houseNumber (exact door point), addressBlock (address-range/segment match incl. interpolated numbers), street, intersection (only returned when requested), place (POI), area (city/district/postal/admin area)

queries.description: Up to 100 forward-geocode queries resolved in a single request

types.description: Default result-type filter applied to every query that does not set its own `types` (houseNumber, addressBlock, street, intersection, place, area)

off.name: geocode_forward
off.description: Convert a free-text address, place name, locality or administrative area into coordinates and a full postal address; tolerates incomplete or partly wrong input. Use geocode_batch for many addresses, place_search for POIs/businesses, geocode_structured when the address components are already separated. Parameters: query (required); optional near {latitude, longitude} or country_codes (strongly recommended - landmark names rank poorly without a location bias), radius_m (with near), bounding_box {west, south, east, north}, limit, language, view, types (houseNumber | addressBlock | street | intersection | place | area). Example: {"query": "1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington DC", "country_codes": ["USA"], "limit": 1}

near.description: Center of the search context; results are ranked around this point

radius_m.description: With `near`: hard-limit results to this radius in meters

country_codes.description: Restrict results to these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, e.g. ["USA","MEX"])

bounding_box.description: Hard-limit results to this bounding box

language.description: Result language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US"

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

types.description: Restrict results to these types: houseNumber (exact door point), addressBlock (address-range/segment match incl. interpolated numbers), street, intersection (only returned when requested), place (POI), area (city/district/postal/admin area)

off.name: geocode_reverse
off.description: Find the nearest address for a coordinate; returns the full postal address, the matched position and a bounding box. Parameters: coordinate {latitude, longitude} (required); optional country_codes, bounding_box {west, south, east, north}, language, view. Example: {"coordinate": {"latitude": 48.8566, "longitude": 2.3522}}

country_codes.description: Restrict results to these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, e.g. ["USA","MEX"])

bounding_box.description: Hard-limit results to this bounding box

language.description: Result language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US"

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

off.name: geocode_structured
off.description: Geocode an address given as separate fields instead of one string; searches addresses and administrative areas only, never POIs. Use when the components are already known and precision matters; otherwise use geocode_forward. Parameters: country_code (required, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3) plus at least one of state, county, city, suburb, neighborhood, street, house_number, postal_code; optional near {latitude, longitude}, limit, types, view. Example: {"country_code": "GBR", "city": "London", "street": "Baker Street", "house_number": "221B"}

country_code.description: Country of the address (required, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, e.g. "USA")

types.description: Restrict results to these types: houseNumber (exact door point), addressBlock (address-range/segment match incl. interpolated numbers), street, intersection (only returned when requested), place (POI), area (city/district/postal/admin area)

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

off.name: get_api_parameters
off.description:
Get structured parameter details for a NextBillion REST API endpoint: type, required, default, allowed values, units and description. More precise than a prose search for questions about one specific parameter. Returns every matching API variant (e.g. directions/flexible and directions/fast), identified by heading_path. Empty units means the documentation does not state a unit. SDK methods are not covered. When the index is temporarily unavailable the result says so and names the public docs site.
Parameters:
- endpoint (string, required unless doc_id given): API slug, optionally with variant, e.g. directions or directions/flexible; a tool name such as geocode_batch or a doc_id also resolves. An unknown endpoint returns found: false with similar endpoints.
- doc_id (string, optional): page id instead of endpoint.
- name (string, optional): one parameter name.
Example: {"endpoint": "directions", "name": "truck_weight"}

endpoint.description: API slug with optional variant (directions, directions/flexible, geofence/create), a tool name (geocode_batch) or a doc_id

off.name: get_documentation
off.description:
Fetch the full text of one documentation page by its doc_id, as returned by search_documentation. Use when an excerpt is not enough to answer accurately. Pages over the size limit return truncated: true and a section list; a single section can be requested with section. Sample request and response bodies are omitted unless include_examples is true. An unknown doc_id or section returns found: false with similar ids or the section list. When the index is temporarily unavailable the result says so and names the public docs site.
Parameters:
- doc_id (string, required): page id from search results.
- section (string, optional): heading of one section to return.
- include_examples (boolean, optional): default false.
Example: {"doc_id": "routing/directions-api/examples/legal-routes-for-a-given-truck-weight"}

doc_id.description: Page id from search_documentation or list_documentation_topics

section.description: Heading (or its anchor) of one section to return

include_examples.description: Include sample request/response code blocks (default false)

off.name: isochrone
off.description: Calculate the area reachable from a point within given travel times or distances; returns a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of contours (geometry coordinates are [longitude, latitude]). Each contour ring can be drawn with static_route_map by passing it as paths[].geojson_coordinates with a fill_color. Documentation for this API is available through search_documentation. Parameters: origin {latitude, longitude} (required); exactly one of contours_minutes (array, up to 4 values, max 40) or contours_meters (array, up to 4 values, max 60000); optional mode, polygons (true for Polygon geometry), denoise, generalize (meters), contours_colors (hex without #, one per contour), departure_time. Example: {"origin": {"latitude": 37.7749, "longitude": -122.4194}, "contours_minutes": [5, 10], "polygons": true}

origin.description: Starting point of the reachability analysis

contours_minutes.description: Travel times in minutes, one contour each (max 4 values, increasing, max 40)

contours_meters.description: Travel distances in meters, one contour each (max 4 values, increasing, max 60000)

polygons.description: Return contours as GeoJSON Polygons instead of LineStrings

denoise.description: Remove contours smaller than this fraction of the largest (default 1: largest only)

departure_time.description: Departure as a UNIX timestamp in seconds, for typical-traffic analysis

contours_colors.description: One hex color (without #) per contour, e.g. ["ff0000", "00ff00"]

generalize.description: Simplification tolerance in meters (Douglas-Peucker); omit for automatic

off.name: list_documentation_topics
off.description:
List the available documentation categories, APIs and pages, with index metadata. Useful before searching, when the right terms are not yet known, e.g. to see which APIs exist for a problem area. When the index is temporarily unavailable the result says so and names the public docs site.
Parameters:
- category (string, optional): limit to one category.
- sdk (string, optional): Android, iOS or Flutter.
Example: {"category": "Optimization"}

sdk.description: Only pages of this platform: Android, iOS, Flutter, Web

off.name: measure
off.description: Measure straight-line (geodesic, WGS84) distance between two points, the length of a line, the area and perimeter of a polygon, or the bearing from one point to another. Straight-line (geodesic) geometry computed locally, not road distance or travel time: for those, directions or distance_matrix apply. No sign-in needed. Parameters: mode (distance | length | area | bearing); from and to ({latitude, longitude}) for distance and bearing; line (array of points) for length; polygon (GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon, e.g. an isochrone contour) for area; units (meters, kilometers, miles, feet, nautical_miles; default meters); area_units (square_meters, square_kilometers, hectares, acres, square_miles, square_feet; default square_meters). Example: {"mode": "distance", "from": {"latitude": 12.9716, "longitude": 77.5946}, "to": {"latitude": 13.0827, "longitude": 80.2707}, "units": "kilometers"}

mode.description: distance: between two points; length: of a line; area: of a polygon; bearing: from one point to another

off.name: nearest
off.description: Find the candidate points nearest to a target as the crow flies (e.g. the closest depots to a customer), or snap the target onto a line and report the closest position on it. Straight-line (geodesic) distances, computed locally, no sign-in needed; distance_matrix gives travel time and road distance instead. Parameters: target ({latitude, longitude}); either candidates (array of {latitude, longitude, id?}) with k (default 1), or line (array of points); units (default meters). Returns ranked {id, point, distance} for candidates, or snapped_point, distance, segment_index and distance_along_line for a line. Example: {"target": {"latitude": 12.9716, "longitude": 77.5946}, "candidates": [{"latitude": 13.0827, "longitude": 80.2707, "id": "Chennai"}, {"latitude": 19.076, "longitude": 72.8777, "id": "Mumbai"}], "k": 1, "units": "kilometers"}

candidates.description: Points to rank by straight-line distance from target

id.description: Optional label echoed back in the result

k.description: How many nearest candidates to return (default 1)

line.description: A line to snap the target onto

off.name: place_browse
off.description: List places of given categories around a location, ranked by distance, without a text query - e.g. all restaurants or schools near a point. Use place_search when the user describes what they want in words; use place_lookup to expand a result by id. Parameters: categories (required array of category names or ids); near {latitude, longitude} (recommended), radius_m (with near), country_codes, bounding_box {west, south, east, north}, limit, language, view. Example: {"categories": ["restaurant"], "near": {"latitude": 1.2839, "longitude": 103.8607}, "radius_m": 800, "limit": 10}

categories.description: Category names or ids to browse; a place matching any of them is returned (e.g. ["restaurant"], ["schools"], ["7376"])

near.description: Center of the search context; results are ranked around this point

radius_m.description: With `near`: hard-limit results to this radius in meters

country_codes.description: Restrict results to these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, e.g. ["USA","MEX"])

bounding_box.description: Hard-limit results to this bounding box

language.description: Result language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US"

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

off.name: place_lookup
off.description: Fetch the full details of a place (address, position, access points, categories, contacts) by its unique id, as returned by place_search, geocode_forward, autosuggest, autocomplete or search_along_route. Parameters: id (required); optional view. Example: {"id": "2EmBgAmFpR9dg0D89EBzNA"}

id.description: Unique place id, as returned by the other place/geocoding tools

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

off.name: place_search
off.description: Search for places, points of interest and businesses with a free-text query (e.g. "gas station", "coffee"), ranked by relevance around a location. Use geocode_forward for plain address-to-coordinates conversion. Documentation for this API is available through search_documentation. Parameters: query (required); optional near {latitude, longitude} (recommended), radius_m (with near), country_codes, bounding_box {west, south, east, north}, limit, language, view. Example: {"query": "coffee", "near": {"latitude": 37.7749, "longitude": -122.4194}, "radius_m": 1000, "limit": 5}

near.description: Center of the search context; results are ranked around this point

radius_m.description: With `near`: hard-limit results to this radius in meters

country_codes.description: Restrict results to these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, e.g. ["USA","MEX"])

bounding_box.description: Hard-limit results to this bounding box

language.description: Result language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US"

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories. Default: Unified (or the requester region)

off.name: points_in_polygon
off.description: Geofencing: tell which of up to 1,000 points lie inside a polygon, for example which delivery addresses fall within an isochrone contour or a service area. Holes are respected; the test is done in map (flat degree) space, matching how polygons are drawn. Computed locally, no sign-in needed. Parameters: polygon (GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon, or an isochrone Feature); points (array of {latitude, longitude, id?}); include_boundary (default true). Returns inside and outside lists (ids, or indexes when no id is given) with counts. Example: {"polygon": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[77.59, 12.97], [77.61, 12.97], [77.61, 12.99], [77.59, 12.99], [77.59, 12.97]]]}, "points": [{"latitude": 12.98, "longitude": 77.6, "id": "A"}]}

polygon.description: A GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon geometry (coordinates in [longitude, latitude] order), or a Feature wrapping one — an isochrone contour can be passed as is

id.description: Optional label echoed back in the result

points.description: Points to test, each optionally with an id

include_boundary.description: Count points exactly on the edge as inside (default true)

off.name: polygon_ops
off.description: Combine polygons: union (merge), intersect (overlap) or difference (first minus the others), for example the overlap of two isochrones or the part of a zone not covered by a depot area. Returns the resulting GeoJSON geometry (Polygon or MultiPolygon, or null when empty) with its geodesic area. Computed locally, no sign-in needed. Parameters: operation (union | intersect | difference); polygons (array of 2–20 GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon geometries, isochrone Features accepted); area_units (default square_meters); max_vertices (default 500, result simplified to fit). Example: {"operation": "intersect", "polygons": [{"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[77.59, 12.97], [77.61, 12.97], [77.61, 12.99], [77.59, 12.99], [77.59, 12.97]]]}, {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[77.6, 12.98], [77.62, 12.98], [77.62, 13.0], [77.6, 13.0], [77.6, 12.98]]]}], "area_units": "hectares"}

operation.description: difference = first polygon minus all others

items.description: A GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon geometry (coordinates in [longitude, latitude] order), or a Feature wrapping one — an isochrone contour can be passed as is

polygons.description: Two or more polygons (GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon or isochrone Features)

max_vertices.description: Simplify the returned shape to at most this many vertices (default 500); the result says when it was simplified

off.name: postcode_lookup
off.description: Get the centroid and boundary polygon of a postal/ZIP code, or find the postal code that contains a coordinate; one lookup per call. Supported countries: USA, India, UK, Netherlands, Austria, Germany, Indonesia, France, Singapore, Philippines, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, Spain. Parameters: either postal_code plus country (name, alpha-2 or alpha-3 code), or coordinate {latitude, longitude}; optional geojson_boundary (true for a GeoJSON boundary). Example: {"postal_code": "90011", "country": "USA"}

postal_code.description: Postal/ZIP code to look up (requires `country`; do not combine with `coordinate`)

country.description: Country of the postal code — name, alpha-2, or alpha-3 ISO code. Required with `postal_code`

coordinate.description: Find the postal code containing this location (alternative to `postal_code`)

geojson_boundary.description: Return the boundary polygon in GeoJSON format instead of the default point-list format

off.name: search_along_route
off.description: Find places matching a text query along a driving route, with the detour time and distance each stop adds - for "find X on the way" questions. Pass the route as an ordered list of waypoints, e.g. the origin, waypoints and destination used with directions. Parameters: route_points (array of {latitude, longitude}, at least 2, required), query (required); optional max_detour_seconds (default 900, max 3600), sort_by (detour_time | detour_offset), limit (max 20), view. Example: {"route_points": [{"latitude": 34.0493, "longitude": -118.2557}, {"latitude": 34.0415, "longitude": -118.231}], "query": "gas station", "max_detour_seconds": 600}

route_points.description: Waypoints defining the route to search along, in travel order

query.description: What to find along the route, e.g. "gas station", "coffee"

max_detour_seconds.description: Max driving time to reach a result after leaving the route (default 900 = 15 min)

sort_by.description: Order by detour driving time, or by distance of the detour point from route start

view.description: Geopolitical view for disputed territories (default: requester region or Unified)

off.name: search_documentation
off.description:
Search NextBillion's official API and SDK documentation. Use for any question about how NextBillion works: calling an API, what a parameter means, which API to use, or SDK setup. Answers come from an index of the official documentation, not from live API calls; when the index is temporarily unavailable the result says so and names the public docs site.
Queries match best with the docs' own terms and exact parameter names (truck_weight, option=flexible) rather than everyday phrasing; when results are thin, other API terms may match. Results are excerpts: get_documentation returns a full page. Each result carries a source_url for citation and related_tools, the name of the tool that performs the operation.
Parameters:
- query (string, required): search terms.
- category (string, optional): e.g. Routing, Places.
- api (string, optional): e.g. Directions.
- sdk (string, optional): Android, iOS or Flutter.
- limit (integer, optional): default 5, max 10.
- include_examples (boolean, optional): default false.
Example: {"query": "truck_size truck_weight routing", "api": "Directions"}

query.description: Search terms, ideally the docs’ own vocabulary

category.description: Boost one category, e.g. Routing, Places

sdk.description: Only pages of this platform: Android, iOS, Flutter, Web

include_examples.description: Also return sample request/response code chunks (default false)

off.name: static_map_image
off.description: Render a static map image centered on a location, with optional markers and line/polygon overlays; returns the image inline (path in the result text). For a map auto-fitted to a route or to overlays, use static_route_map. Parameters: center {latitude, longitude} and zoom (0-22) (required); optional markers (array of {latitude, longitude, color, icon_url, anchor, scale}), paths (array of {points [{latitude, longitude}] OR geojson_coordinates [[longitude, latitude], ...], stroke_color, stroke_width, fill_color for a filled polygon}), width, height (default 512), style (streets | light | dark | hybrid), format (png | jpg | webp), retina. Example: {"center": {"latitude": 48.8566, "longitude": 2.3522}, "zoom": 14, "markers": [{"latitude": 48.8584, "longitude": 2.2945, "color": "red"}], "paths": [{"points": [{"latitude": 48.85, "longitude": 2.29}, {"latitude": 48.86, "longitude": 2.30}], "stroke_color": "green"}]}

zoom.description: Zoom level (0 = world, ~10 = city, ~15 = streets; fractional values allowed)

markers.description: Markers to draw, each with optional color or custom icon

color.description: Marker color, e.g. "red" or "#0000ff" (ignored when icon_url is set)

icon_url.description: URL of a custom marker image (max 64 kB / 4096 px, e.g. 64x64 PNG)

anchor.description: Anchor point of a custom icon (default bottom)

paths.description: Extra lines/polygons to draw (e.g. isochrone contours as filled polygons)

geojson_coordinates.description: Vertices as GeoJSON [longitude, latitude] pairs - pass an isochrone or GeoJSON ring here unchanged

fill_color.description: Fill color for a closed shape, e.g. "rgba(255,0,0,0.3)" or "#ff000055"; omit for a line

items.description: A line or filled polygon overlay

retina.description: Render at @2x resolution for high-DPI displays

off.name: static_route_map
off.description: Render a static map auto-fitted to a route and/or overlays: a route from directions, and/or lines and filled polygons such as isochrone contours; very long geometry is simplified automatically to fit the map API URL limit (distances unaffected). Returns the image inline. Parameters: at least one of encoded_polyline (the geometry string from directions, preferred), route_points (array of {latitude, longitude}) or paths (array of {points OR geojson_coordinates [[longitude, latitude], ...], stroke_color, stroke_width, fill_color}); optional markers (array of {latitude, longitude, color, icon_url, anchor, scale}), stroke_color, stroke_width (route line), padding, width, height, style, format, retina. The example draws isochrone contours. Example: {"paths": [{"geojson_coordinates": [[-122.42, 37.77], [-122.40, 37.78], [-122.41, 37.79], [-122.42, 37.77]], "fill_color": "rgba(29,78,216,0.35)", "stroke_color": "#1d4ed8"}], "markers": [{"latitude": 37.7749, "longitude": -122.4194, "color": "red"}]}

encoded_polyline.description: Route geometry as a Google encoded polyline (precision 5) — exactly what the directions tool returns with its default geometry setting

route_points.description: Alternative to encoded_polyline: the route as an ordered list of coordinates

markers.description: Extra markers, e.g. origin and destination, with optional color or custom icon

color.description: Marker color, e.g. "red" or "#0000ff" (ignored when icon_url is set)

icon_url.description: URL of a custom marker image (max 64 kB / 4096 px, e.g. 64x64 PNG)

anchor.description: Anchor point of a custom icon (default bottom)

paths.description: Extra lines/polygons to draw (e.g. isochrone contours as filled polygons)

geojson_coordinates.description: Vertices as GeoJSON [longitude, latitude] pairs - pass an isochrone or GeoJSON ring here unchanged

fill_color.description: Fill color for a closed shape, e.g. "rgba(255,0,0,0.3)" or "#ff000055"; omit for a line

items.description: A line or filled polygon overlay

padding.description: Margin around the route as a fraction of image size (default 0.1)

retina.description: Render at @2x resolution for high-DPI displays

drk.name: geocode_forward
drk.description: Convert an address, place name, or locality into geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude). Use this when the user knows the name or address of a place and needs its coordinates. When include_map: true is passed, you MUST embed the returned map_image_markdown (or ![Location Map](map_image_url)) in your final response text so the map renders in the main chat window.

query.description: The address or place name to geocode. Examples: 'Eiffel Tower, Paris', '1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA', 'Times Square'

at.description: Anchor coordinates to bias results toward a specific area. Format: 'lat,lon' e.g. '37.7749,-122.4194'

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code(s) to restrict results, comma-separated. Examples: 'USA', 'GBR', 'USA,CAN'

language.description: IETF language tag for response language. Examples: 'en', 'fr', 'de'

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 1

language.description: IETF language tag for response language. Examples: 'en', 'fr'

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 1

drk.description: Retrieve geographical coordinates and boundaries for a specific postal/ZIP code.

language.description: IETF language tag for response language. Example: 'en'

language.description: IETF language tag for response language. Example: 'en'

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code(s), comma-separated. Example: 'USA'

language.description: IETF language tag for response language. Example: 'en'

max_detour_time.description: Maximum allowable detour time in seconds from the original route to reach a POI. Example: 600 (10 minutes)

limit.description: Maximum number of POI results to return

categories.description: Comma-separated list of category IDs to filter POIs

drk.name: get_directions
drk.description:
Get turn-by-turn driving, walking, cycling, or truck directions between an origin and a destination. Supports waypoints (intermediate stops), route preferences (avoid tolls/highways), and optional truck-specific constraints.

When 'include_map: true' is passed, the tool generates a static map image. You MUST embed the returned 'map_image_markdown' (or '![Route Map](map_image_url)') in your final assistant response text so the map renders in the main chat response window.

Use the 'flexible' option for:
- Real-time traffic-aware routing
- Truck-specific dimensions and weight constraints
- Shortest vs fastest route comparison
- Hazardous cargo routing
- Advanced avoid preferences

waypoints.description: Intermediate stops between origin and destination. Pipe-separated 'lat,lon' values. Example: '35.6762,139.6503|34.6937,135.5023'. Maximum 50 waypoints via GET (200 via POST).

option.description: Set to 'flexible' for real-time traffic, truck parameters, and advanced routing options. Omit for the Fast API (historical traffic, lower latency).

alternatives.description: Return alternative routes in addition to the best route

avoid.description: Road features or maneuvers to avoid. Pipe-separated values. Options: 'toll', 'highway', 'ferry', 'uturn', 'service_road'. Example: 'toll|highway'

route_type.description: Route optimization strategy (Flexible API only). Default: 'fastest'

departure_time.description: Unix timestamp for planned departure time. Used for traffic-aware routing. Example: 1700000000

steps.description: Include step-by-step turn-by-turn instructions in the response

overview.description: Overview polyline detail level. Default: simplified

language.description: IETF language tag for turn-by-turn instructions. Example: 'en', 'fr'

truck_size.description: Truck dimensions as 'length,width,height' in centimeters (Flexible + mode=truck only). Max: 5000cm × 5000cm × 1000cm. Example: '1200,250,400'

truck_weight.description: Total truck weight including cargo in kilograms (Flexible + mode=truck only). Maximum: 100,000 kg

truck_axle_count.description: Number of truck axles (Flexible + mode=truck only)

truck_hazmat_type.description: Hazardous material classification for truck routing (Flexible + mode=truck only)

emission_type.description: Emission classification standard (Flexible + mode=truck only). Examples: 'euro1', 'euro2', 'euro3', 'euro4', 'euro5', 'euro6'

include_map.description: Generate and embed a static map image showing the calculated route and markers. Default: false

drk.name: distance_matrix
drk.description:
Compute a matrix of travel times and distances between multiple origin and destination locations. Returns time (seconds) and distance (meters) for every origin–destination pair.

Use cases:
- Finding the nearest warehouse to multiple customers
- Comparing ETAs between delivery hubs and stops
- Fleet routing pre-processing

Use the 'flexible' option for real-time traffic, truck-specific routing, or advanced constraints.

Limits:
- Fast API: up to 1,000 × 1,000 origin/destination pairs (default)
- Flexible API: up to 50 × 50 pairs (2,500 elements)

origins.description: List of origin locations. Each must have lat and lon fields.

destinations.description: List of destination locations. Each must have lat and lon fields.

option.description: Set to 'flexible' for real-time traffic, truck parameters, and advanced routing. Omit for Fast API (historical traffic, high volume).

avoid.description: Road features to avoid. Pipe-separated values. Options: 'toll', 'highway', 'ferry'. Example: 'toll'

departure_time.description: Unix timestamp for planned departure. Used for traffic-aware ETA calculations.

truck_size.description: Truck dimensions as 'length,width,height' in centimeters (Flexible + mode=truck only). Max: 5000cm × 5000cm × 1000cm

truck_weight.description: Total truck weight including cargo in kilograms (Flexible + mode=truck only). Maximum: 100,000 kg

drk.name: isochrone
drk.description:
Calculate reachable areas (contours) from a starting location based on driving time (minutes) or driving distance (meters). Returns GeoJSON contours suitable for mapping serviceable delivery or travel zones.

By default, this tool automatically renders a static map image of the calculated isochrone contours overlaying a map. You MUST embed the returned 'map_image_markdown' (or '![Isochrone Map](map_image_url)') in your final assistant response text so the map renders in the main chat response window.

Use cases:
- Defining service coverage zones around a hub or store
- Visualising 5/10/15-minute delivery radiuses
- Analyzing reachable areas for different travel modes (car, truck, walk, bicycle)

Limits:
- contours_minutes: up to 4 contours, maximum 40 minutes per contour
- contours_meters: up to 4 contours, maximum 60,000 meters per contour
- Only one of contours_minutes or contours_meters should be provided per request.

contours_minutes.description: Time threshold(s) in minutes for isochrone contours. Single value or comma-separated values (up to 4 contours, max 40 min). Example: '5' or '5,10,15'

contours_meters.description: Distance threshold(s) in meters for isochrone contours. Single value or comma-separated values (up to 4 contours, max 60000m). Example: '1000' or '1000,5000,10000'

denoise.description: Denoise factor between 0 and 1 to suppress isolated, unreachable pockets. Lower values produce detailed exact contours.

generalize.description: Tolerance in meters for polyline simplification (Douglas-Peucker algorithm).

polygons.description: Set to true to return GeoJSON polygons, or false for linestring contours.

depart_at.description: Unix timestamp for planned departure time. Used for traffic-aware isochrone calculations.

avoid.description: Road features to avoid. Pipe-separated values. Options: 'toll', 'highway', 'ferry'. Example: 'toll|highway'

truck_size.description: Truck dimensions as 'length,width,height' in centimeters (mode=truck only). Example: '1200,250,400'

truck_weight.description: Total truck weight including cargo in kilograms (mode=truck only). Maximum: 100,000 kg

include_map.description: Generate and embed a static map image of the isochrone contours. Default: true

include_geojson.description: Include full raw GeoJSON coordinate arrays in text output. Default: false (returns clean summary)

map_id.description: Map style for the static map image ('streets', 'hybrid', 'dark', 'light'). Default: 'streets'

drk.name: navigation
drk.description:
Get turn-by-turn driving instructions between an origin and a destination using NextBillion's Navigation API. Supports Fast ('option: fast') and Flexible ('option: flexible') versions with live/historical traffic, waypoints (intermediate stops), route preferences (avoid tolls/highways/sharp_turn), and truck-specific parameters.

When 'include_map: true' is passed, the tool generates a static map image. You MUST embed the returned 'map_image_markdown' (or '![Route Map](map_image_url)') in your final assistant response text so the map renders in the main chat response window.

waypoints.description: Intermediate stops between origin and destination. Pipe-separated 'lat,lon' values. Example: '35.6762,139.6503|34.6937,135.5023'. Maximum 50 waypoints via GET (200 via POST).

option.description: Set to 'flexible' for real-time traffic, truck parameters, and advanced routing options (default). Set to 'fast' for low-latency standard navigation.

alternatives.description: Return alternative routes in addition to the best route

avoid.description: Road features or maneuvers to avoid. Pipe-separated values. Options: 'toll', 'highway', 'ferry', 'uturn', 'sharp_turn', 'service_road'. Example: 'toll|highway'

route_type.description: Route optimization strategy (Flexible API only). Default: 'fastest'

departure_time.description: Unix timestamp for planned departure time. Used for traffic-aware routing. Example: 1700000000

steps.description: Include step-by-step turn-by-turn instructions in the response

overview.description: Overview polyline detail level. Default: simplified

language.description: IETF language tag for turn-by-turn instructions. Example: 'en', 'fr'

truck_size.description: Truck dimensions as 'length,width,height' in centimeters (mode=truck only). Example: '1200,250,400'

truck_weight.description: Total truck weight including cargo in kilograms (mode=truck only).

truck_hazmat_type.description: Hazardous material classification for truck routing (mode=truck only). Example: "circumstantial"

include_map.description: Generate and embed a static map image showing the calculated route and markers. Default: false

drk.name: snap_to_roads
drk.description:
Snap raw GPS coordinates (path) to the nearest navigable road network using NextBillion's Snap to Roads API. Corrects noisy GPS trajectories and returns snapped road coordinates and optional interpolated route geometry.

When 'include_map: true' is passed, the tool generates a static map image showing the snapped path and markers. You MUST embed the returned 'map_image_markdown' (or '![Snapped Path Map](map_image_url)') in your final assistant response text.

path.description: Sequence of GPS coordinates to snap to roads. Format: Pipe-separated 'lat,lon' pairs. Example: '34.0263,-118.3135|34.0502,-118.2989'.

interpolate.description: Interpolate and return full snapped route geometry between path coordinates

radiuses.description: Custom search radius per coordinate point in meters. Format: Pipe-separated integers. Example: '5|10|5'

timestamps.description: Unix timestamps corresponding to each path coordinate. Format: Pipe-separated integers. Example: '1600000000|1600000060'

overview.description: Overview geometry detail level. Default: simplified

include_map.description: Generate and embed a static map image showing the snapped route path and markers. Default: false

drk.name: route_report
drk.description:
Generate a comprehensive mileage and trip report for a route geometry using NextBillion's Route Report API. Provides trip duration, distance covered broken down by state, country, and road class, along with segment max speeds, toll info, bridges, tunnels, and maneuvers.

When 'include_map: true' is passed, the tool generates a static map image showing the route polyline. You MUST embed the returned 'map_image_markdown' (or '![Route Report Map](map_image_url)') in your final assistant response text.

original_shape.description: The route geometry string (encoded polyline) or geometry coordinate array/object representing the trip path.

original_shape_type.description: Encoding format of the original_shape. Options: 'polyline', 'polyline6', 'geojson'. Default: 'polyline'

include_map.description: Generate and embed a static map image showing the reported route path. Default: false

drk.name: get_static_map
drk.description:
Generate a non-interactive static map image (PNG, JPG, or WebP) centered on coordinates, bounding box, or auto-fitted to paths and markers.

You MUST embed the returned 'map_image_markdown' (or '![Static Map](map_image_url)') in your final assistant response text so the map renders directly in the main chat response window.

Use cases:
- Rendering maps in chats or reports without needing client-side JavaScript mapping libraries.
- Visualizing routes, boundaries, clusters, and point locations on a customized map.
- Generating map snapshots for export or notification cards.

mode.description: Image positioning strategy: 'auto' (fits all markers/paths), 'center' (requires center + zoom), or 'bounds' (requires miny,minx,maxy,maxx)

center.description: Center coordinates for 'center' mode. Format: 'lat,lon'. Example: '37.7749,-122.4194'

zoom.description: Zoom level (0 to 20) for 'center' mode. Example: 12

bounds.description: Bounding box for 'bounds' mode. Format: 'miny,minx,maxy,maxx' (minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon). Example: '33.93,-118.12,34.10,-117.90'

width.description: Width of the output map image in pixels (max 2048). Default: 600

height.description: Height of the output map image in pixels (max 2048). Default: 400

scale.description: Set to '@2x' for high-resolution retina displays

drk.name: reconstruct_route
drk.description:
Reconstruct a map-matched, accurate route path from a sequence of raw or sparse GPS waypoints.

Unlike other tracking tools, this tool automatically generates and returns a static map image rendered in the chat response window alongside the route geometry data.

waypoints.description: Sequence of GPS waypoints to reconstruct. Format: pipe-separated "lat1,lon1|lat2,lon2|lat3,lon3" (e.g. "34.0493,-118.2557|34.0471,-118.2497|34.0388,-118.2075")

round_trip.description: Whether the reconstructed trip returns to the starting point

show_map.description: Whether to generate and attach a static map image preview in the response (default: true)

map_id.description: Map style for static image preview ("streets", "hybrid", "dark", "light")

width.description: Width of static map image in pixels

height.description: Height of static map image in pixels

drk.name: driver_assignment_sync
drk.description: Assign drivers to orders/tasks in real-time (synchronously). Best for immediate ride-hailing or localized dispatch. Accepts lists of orders and available vehicles, returning trip assignments, unassigned orders, and available vehicles immediately. Maximum 200 orders and 100 vehicles per request.

orders.description: List of orders to fulfill. Each order object should include location/pickup/dropoff coordinates, optional attributes, priority, or time windows.

vehicles.description: List of available drivers/vehicles. Each vehicle object should specify current location, remaining waypoints, capacity, attributes, etc.

filter.description: Filtering criteria to constrain matching. Maximum radius: 10000m, pickup_eta: 3600s, driving_distance: 10000m.

options.description: Cost and optimization options (e.g. cost model, calculation type).

dropoff_details.description: Set to true to return complete drop-off steps for assigned trips.

drk.name: driver_assignment_async_submit
drk.description: Submit a driver assignment optimization problem asynchronously for larger fleets or wide geographic areas (up to 200km radius, 8-hour ETA limit). Returns a solution ID string which can be polled using get_driver_assignment_result.

orders.description: List of orders (up to 200) with locations and constraints.

vehicles.description: List of available vehicles/drivers (up to 100) with locations and capacities.

filter.description: Extended filtering criteria (radius up to 200,000m, pickup_eta up to 28,800s, driving_distance up to 700,000m).

dropoff_details.description: Include dropoff steps in calculated trip details.

drk.name: get_driver_assignment_result
drk.description: Retrieve the calculated solution for an asynchronous driver assignment job submitted via driver_assignment_async_submit.

id.description: The unique solution ID returned by driver_assignment_async_submit.

drk.name: cluster_jobs
drk.description:
Bundle orders or jobs together into geographic or capacity-optimized clusters to minimize travel distance or service duration. Returns a unique job ID to retrieve results using get_clustering_result.

FORMAT SPECIFICATION:
- 'locations': Array of coordinate string pairs ["lat,lon", "lat,lon", ...]. Example: ["34.0522,-118.2437", "34.0407,-118.2468"]
- 'jobs': Array of job objects. Each object MUST have an integer 'id', 0-indexed 'location_index', and scalar number 'quantity' (e.g. 1, NOT an array [1]). Example: [{ "id": 1, "location_index": 0, "quantity": 1 }]
- 'clusters': Array of target cluster definitions with integer 'id' and scalar 'capacity' number (e.g. 2, NOT an array [2]). Example: [{ "id": 1, "capacity": 2 }, { "id": 2, "capacity": 2 }]

locations.description: Locations for clustering. Array of coordinate strings ["lat,lon", ...] or location objects.

jobs.description: List of job objects with integer id, 0-indexed location_index, and scalar quantity (e.g. 1).

clusters.description: List of target cluster objects specifying integer id and scalar capacity (e.g. 2).

routing.description: Routing preferences and vehicle constraints (e.g. mode, truck_size, truck_weight).

options.description: Objective and clustering options (e.g. travel_cost: distance/duration, max_cluster_radius).

description.description: Optional descriptive label for the clustering job.

drk.name: get_clustering_result
drk.description: Retrieve the result and optimal groupings of a clustering job submitted via cluster_jobs using its task ID.

id.description: The unique task ID returned when submitting cluster_jobs.

drk.name: get_road_segments
drk.description:
Retrieve comprehensive details for all road segments within a specified circular or bounding box geographic region, including segment shapes, midpoints, max speed, and direction of travel.

Use cases:
- Extracting road segment metadata and speed limits for map displays or analytics.
- Evaluating speed profiles and directional properties across geographic bounds.

type.description: Query area mode: 'circle' (center + radius) or 'bbox' (min/max lat/lon)

circle.description: Circle parameters. Required when type is 'circle'

bbox.description: Bounding box parameters (max diagonal 100km). Required when type is 'bbox'

drk.name: get_traffic_incidents
drk.description:
Retrieve active traffic incidents and road closures for a specified bounding box region or specific incident IDs. Returns cause, impacted roads, severity, and travel delays.

Use cases:
- Monitoring live traffic disruptions and closures for fleet operations.
- Inspecting specific traffic incident IDs for disruption analysis.

bbox.description: Bounding box coordinates formatted as 'min_lon,min_lat,max_lon,max_lat' (max area 10,000 km²). Example: '-83.16,39.90,-82.90,40.09'

id.description: Optional incident ID or array of incident IDs to filter by (max 5 IDs)

drk.name: get_hourly_weather_forecast
drk.description:
Get hour-by-hour weather forecast information for a specified location up to 24 hours into the future. Returns temperature, precipitation, wind speed, humidity, and UV index.

Use cases:
- Hourly dispatch planning and weather risk mitigation.
- Short-term delivery route planning and driver safety checks.

at.description: Target location coordinates formatted as 'lat,lng'. Example: '52.37,4.9'

forecast_hours.description: Number of hours to forecast into the future (max 24). Example: 6

drk.name: get_daily_weather_forecast
drk.description:
Get day-by-day weather forecast information for a specified location up to 14 days into the future. Returns min/max temperatures, precipitation, wind, UV index, and sun/moon timings.

Use cases:
- Long-range fleet planning and multi-day haul scheduling.
- Field operations and seasonal weather risk assessment.

at.description: Target location coordinates formatted as 'lat,lng'. Example: '52.37,4.9'

forecast_days.description: Number of days to forecast into the future (max 14). Example: 7

drk.name: get_regional_weather
drk.description:
Retrieve real-time and predicted regional weather radar precipitation information formatted as GeoJSON polygons for a specified region.

Use cases:
- Visualizing regional storm fronts, precipitation cells, and weather hazards on maps.
- Analyzing weather impacts across large geographic operating zones.

drk.name: create_road_restriction
drk.description:
Create a new custom road restriction (e.g. closure, maxspeed, turn restriction, fixedspeed, truck restriction, or parking restriction) for road segments, nodes, or a geofence using the Road Editor API.

Use cases:
- Adding custom road closures or speed limit overrides to customize fleet routing.
- Defining vehicle-specific or turn restrictions in targeted operational areas.

name.description: Human-readable name or label for the restriction

comment.description: Optional comment or reason for the restriction

geofence.description: Geofence polygon object defining restriction area

segments.description: List of road segments affected (can be segment IDs or objects with from/to node IDs)

nodes.description: List of node IDs affected by the restriction

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

drk.name: update_road_restriction
drk.description:
Update attributes of an existing road restriction by its ID using the Road Editor API.

Use cases:
- Modifying restriction properties, schedules, or names.

id.description: Unique ID of the restriction to update

comment.description: Updated comment or reason for the restriction

mode.description: Updated travel modes affected by the restriction

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

drk.name: set_road_restriction_state
drk.description:
Set the active state of a restriction (enabled, disabled, or deleted) by its ID using the Road Editor API.

Use cases:
- Temporarily disabling or re-enabling custom road restrictions without deleting them.
- Soft-deleting obsolete restriction records.

id.description: Unique ID of the restriction

state.description: Target state of the restriction: 'enabled', 'disabled', or 'deleted'

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

drk.name: search_road_restrictions_in_bbox
drk.description:
Fetch a list of active road restrictions that fall within a specified geographic bounding box.

Use cases:
- Querying restrictions in a map viewport or bounding box during route planning.
- Auditing active road edits in a targeted geographic region.

restriction_type.description: Filter by restriction type (e.g. closure, maxspeed)

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

drk.name: get_road_restriction
drk.description:
Retrieve details of a specific road restriction by its unique ID.

Use cases:
- Inspecting restriction attributes, boundary details, and current status.

id.description: Unique restriction ID

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

drk.name: list_road_restrictions
drk.description:
Get a paginated list of road restrictions filtered by area, type, or status using the Road Editor API.

Use cases:
- Displaying paginated lists of road restrictions in management portals or tables.
- Filtering restrictions by operational area or restriction type.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 15)

area.description: Filter by area code (e.g. california, singapore)

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

drk.name: delete_road_restriction
drk.description:
Permanently delete a specific road restriction using its unique ID.

Use cases:
- Removing obsolete or expired road restriction configurations.

id.description: Unique ID of the restriction to delete

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

drk.name: get_road_editor_areas
drk.description:
Get the list of available geographic areas configured for the Road Editor API.

Use cases:
- Discovering valid area identifiers and supported travel modes for adding restrictions.

base_url.description: Custom Road Editor API base URL if applicable

limit.description: Maximum number of documentation results to return
